interest: The file provides historians with exceptional documentation on the tension between demilitarizing and democratizing Japanese science—spearheaded by the landmark Roger Adams mission—and Allied exploitation of Japanese industrial and technical knowledge. It uniquely details inter-Allied diplomatic and legal conflicts over technical intelligence and seized German assets, such as Australia's contested inspection of the Wacker acetic anhydride process, alongside domestic scientific dissent over cyclotron destruction. Furthermore, SCAP media analyses of Japanese public attitudes toward science and security dossiers on figures like Roy Hoko Ikeda highlight the intersection of postwar scientific rehabilitation with emerging Cold War anti-communist priorities.
overview: This file documents United States and Allied occupation policy regarding Japanese science, technology, industrial processes, and scientific institutions from October 1945 to August 1949. Central to the collection are interagency and diplomatic deliberations involving SCAP, the State Department, SANACC, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Far Eastern Commission regarding Allied access to pre-1946 Japanese technological and commercial processes, formalized through policies such as FEC-280 and SCAPIN 1925. The records capture negotiations with partner nations including the United Kingdom, Australia, Norway, and the Netherlands, highlighting legal disputes over vested German external assets like the Wacker acetic anhydride process, as well as protests by the Federation of American Scientists against cyclotron destruction and nuclear research controls. In addition, the file includes the 1947 report by the Dr. Roger Adams Scientific Advisory Group on democratizing Japanese scientific administration and higher education, SCAP analyses of Japanese public attitudes toward science, and security investigations concerning Roy Hoko Ikeda's proposed anti-communist research institute.
